question.leadin: This person names an "exchange" that transferred plants, animals, and diseases between Europe and the Americas.
question.text: Name this Genoese explorer, who "discovered" the New World in 1492 with the ships Nina [NEEN-yah], Pinta, and Santa Maria.
question.clue: Francisco de Bobadilla replaced this man as Governor of the Indies after accusations of tyranny in Hispaniola.

swap.leadin: Identify some figures related to the Napoleonic Wars.
swap.text: This elder brother of Napoleon was the King of Naples and Sicily and later became the King of Spain because his younger brother believed in nepotism.
swap.clue: Joachim Murat succeeded this man when he abruptly left the throne of Naples.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Counter-Reformation.
question.text: This institution of the Counter-Reformation, whose first chief was Tomas de Torquemada, was established by Isabella I of Castile to root out Moriscos, Jews, and non-Catholics.
question.answerHtml: Spanish Inquisition [or Tribunal of the Holy Office of the Inquisition]
question.clue: Tomas de Torquemada led this organization, which used a seal that quoted Psalm 73, and frequently used the auto-da-fe to publicly burn heretics.

swap.text: The Umayyad Caliphate would later be expelled by the Abbasids, but it maintained its rule on this peninsula. Christians on this peninsula would later lead a campaign against the Muslims called the Reconquista.
swap.clue: The knight El Cid fought on both sides of a series of military campaigns in this region, which concluded in 1492 with the fall of the Emirate of Granada.

question.text: The Christian reconquest of Iberia was completed by Ferdinand of Aragon and his wife, this queen of Castile.
question.clue: This mother of Juana the Mad conquered the kingdom of Granada and, along with her husband, expelled all Jews from their lands through the Alhambra Decree.

swap.text: This Dominican friar was the first Grand Inquisitor, becoming infamous for his zeal and cruelty.
swap.clue: This confessor of Isabella also led the the Spanish Inquisition as the Grand Inquisitor.

question.leadin: This war began with a coup against the Second Republic, which was launched by several generals in July of 1936.
question.text: Name this war in which Republican forces lost to Francisco Franco's Nationalists.
question.answerHtml: Spanish Civil War [or Guerra Civil Española; or Fourth Carlist War; or Cuarta Guerra Carlista]
question.clue: Germany supported one side in this conflict with the Condor Legion.

swap.text: ETA ("etuh") seeks independence for this region of Spain. This region's namesake language is an isolate that has a pidgin with Icelandic due to meetings between whalers from this region and Icelandic fishermen.
swap.clue: The GAL, an illegal paramilitary group founded by the government of F´elipe Gonzalez, once operated in this region to fight the ETA, a terrorist group that promoted this region's separation.

question.text: The successor to Pedro Gonzales de Mendoza as the Archbishop of Toledo, this advisor to Isabella was eventually promoted to Grand Inquisitor after he brokered the Agreement of Salamanca, ending a potential succession crisis involving Philip I of Castile. In his later years he led a crusade against the Muslim held city of Oran.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the Sale Corsairs.
swap.text: The Sale Corsairs were based out of New Sale, a city founded after Philip III expelled these people from Spain in 1610. This Spanish term refers to the Muslims who stayed in Spain after the reconquest and converted to Christianity.
swap.answerHtml: Moriscos [do not accept terms like "Moors" or "Muslims" that are not Spanish]
swap.clue: This silk trade-controlling group created the maritime Republic of Sale (SAL-ay), and unsuccessfully sought aid from the Huguenot stronghold of Bearn.

question.text: Before the founding of the UAW, automotive workers got into a battle named after this city during a strike against Electric Auto-Lite. A war named after this city resulted from a dispute about the southern border of Michigan.
question.clue: The third council in this city confirmed Reccared's decision to convert from Arianism to Catholicism.

swap.text: Members of this ethnic group were particularly active in the whaling industry, setting up a fishing village at Red Bay in Labrador. Whalers from this ethnic group were killed in a 1615 massacre perpetrated by locals in Iceland.
swap.clue: This ethnic group's whaling activities led to the creation of a pidgin described by Jon Olafsson, and 32 shipwrecked members of this ethnic group were murdered in Iceland in the 1615 "Slaying of the Spaniards."

question.leadin: This autonomous community contains the provinces of Malaga and Cadiz.
question.text: Name this southernmost autonomous community of Spain that contains the city of Granada.
question.clue: This region is also home to the city of Cadiz, which, owing to its strategic position, was raided by Sir Francis Drake seeking to impede the Spanish Armada and blockaded by Lord Nelson before the Battle of Trafalgar.

swap.leadin: Ringtones featuring this person's voice became popular after he interrupted Hugo Chavez, asking him, "Why don't you shut up?"
swap.text: Name this ruler of Spain from 1975 to 2014, when he abdicated in favor of his son Felipe VI. This ruler oversaw the Spanish transition to democracy.
swap.clue: This head of state asked Hugo Chavez "Why don't you shut up?" at a meeting where Chavez repeatedly interrupted one of his countrymen.

question.text: The Flight of Earls aimed to secure the support of this ruler, who unfortunately was unwilling to intervene after making peace with his British counterpart, James I, in 1604. His father sent the Spanish Armada to raid Britain.
question.answerHtml: Philip III of Spain [or Felipe III; or Philip the Pious; prompt on “Philip”]
question.clue: Through the secret Onate (oh-NYAH-tay) treaty, this king renounced claims to Bohemia and Hungary and, in return, agreed to back his relative Ferdinand II, leading to his intervention against the "Winter King".

swap.text: The formation of a coalition government with the far-right CEDA party during the Second Republic era led socialists and anarchists to organize a 1934 general strike in this province of Spain, during which miners marched and captured the capital.
swap.clue: This kingdom ended when its ruler moved out of its last capital at Oviedo in the Cantabrian Mountains.

question.text: After the war, Philip V issued this set of laws that removed the autonomy of regions that were formerly part of the Aragonese crown, including abolishing the traditional charters of Valencia and Catalonia, in an attempt to create a centralized Spanish state.
question.clue: Carlism gained major support from Basque and Catalan communities by promising to reverse these laws of Philip V, which revoked the autonomy of Spain's peripheral communities.

swap.text: This Basque-born commander of Carlist forces won such battles as Venta de Echavarri and Alsasua before tension with Don Carlos led to his downfall.

question.text: Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera's sister Pilar headed this subset of the Falange Party that organized cooking lessons and published cookbooks to reinforce traditionalist gender norms.

swap.text: This socialist served as Azana's prime minister and minister of war during the first two years of the war, after which he was replaced by Juan Negrin.
